newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner profit up 40 pct, beats forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner profit up 40 pct, beats forecasts.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG Thursday reported a surge in 1996 operating profits of more than 40 percent, outperforming its top domestic rivals in part due to proceeds from dissolving hidden reserves.

Dresdner, Germany's second-largest bank said operating profit after risk provisions rose to more than 2.8 billion German marks ($1.65 billion) from 1.99 billion ($1.17 billion), according to preliminary data.
Analysts had expected a smaller rise in operating profit, by 30 percent to about 2.6 billion ($1.534 billion).
Dresdner's earnings were partly driven by British investment bank unit Kleinwort Benson, included in results for the full year in 1996 compared with just three months in 1995.
Dresdner is also expected to have received a late boost in commission income for its part in the stock offering of state telephone monopoly Deutsche Telekom AG in November.
Dresdner did not give a net profit figure which analysts forecasted would rise 30 percent to about 1.57 billion marks ($926 million). Final results will be reported in April.
